text: Businesses rethink strategies as AI empowers consumers

HÀ NỘI - Artificial intelligence (AI) and intelligent agents are booming, reshaping consumer behaviour and forcing CEOs, directors and business leaders to rethink how they work and develop their businesses.

The 10th Việt Nam Sales and Marketing Congress (VSMCamp), alongside the senior summit for sales and marketing directors (CSMOSummit), is being held in Hà Nội to discuss these changes and help the business community adapt to the evolving landscape.

Organised by CSMO Việt Nam, under the Vietnam Association of Corporate Directors, in collaboration with Le Bros, the November 19-20 event has attracted about 1,500 participants from businesses, agencies, academia, training organisations and strategy consultancies.
For years, sales and marketing have followed a straightforward playbook: craft a message, reach out, and persuade - relying entirely on human decision-makers to close the deal.
However, the emergence of intelligent agents (AI agents) is fundamentally altering this dynamic.

AI is evolving from a tool that merely supports data analysis into an intermediary layer capable of directly searching for and comparing products, assessing risks, and even executing transactions on behalf of consumers.

Themed The Agentic Marketplace: When AI Joins the Power of Choice, the event brings together over 70 prominent speakers across 50 presentations and panels, creating a strategic forum on how businesses must adapt as consumers increasingly delegate buying decisions to AI.
At the same time, businesses must establish a position that earns the trust of consumers, gains recognition from the platform, and secures recommendations from AI algorithms.

Lê Quốc Vinh, president of CSMO Việt Nam and Le Bros, said: "Where technology once helped brands understand and reach customers, AI agents are now fundamentally shifting the landscape, stepping directly into the decision-making process itself.
"This forces businesses to rethink how they earn trust and structure their growth teams.
Entering a new decade, VSMCamp & CSMOSummit aim to bridge global insights with the realities of the Vietnamese market, equipping professionals to proactively shape what comes next.

The speakers' insights are structured around three key discussion tracks at VSMCamp 2026: standardising verified data to ensure AI accurately interprets brand value; optimising presence for AI-driven search (GEO) while integrating brand sentiment; and breaking down functional silos to unify Marketing, Sales, and Customer Service into a continuous growth ecosystem.

In his presentation titled Design for a Trusted Brand - Trust in the Age of AI Disruption, Nguyễn Đức Sơn, founder & chairman of Interloka Brand Agency, argues that brands must establish a clear identity and verifiable, distinctive values, while maintaining a "human touch" to build trust in the era of AI disruption.
Arjun Ganesh, director of Solution Engineering for APAC, highlights a shift in the field of Search Engine Optimisation (SEO).

In his presentation themed "Answers instead of links, summaries instead of visits, selection instead of ranking", he argued that as AI emerges as the new "gatekeeper", brands must go beyond merely being discoverable; they must also be selected and recommended by AI, based on a foundation of structured, comprehensive, and reliable information.
Nguyễn Việt Đức, CEO of Unica Solutions JSC, focuses on the challenge of re-architecting growth systems for the era of AI agents.

"In the age of the 'Agentic Marketplace', competitive advantage does not belong to the company that purchases the most expensive AI model; rather, victory goes to the organisation that possesses an open infrastructure, clean data, and an architecture designed for autonomous operations," Đức explains.
He proposes the "One Growth System" model, a framework that integrates data and activities across marketing, sales, and customer service into a unified "Single Customer View.
This approach facilitates synchronised operations and enables the gradual delegation of decision-making authority to AI.
In the second day, CSMOSummit 2026 focuses on the transformation requirements at the leadership and corporate governance levels.

Topics such as building AI-native enterprises, agentic commerce, restructuring growth systems, and defining the boundaries of AI's autonomous authority further expand the conversation on how businesses can prepare for a market increasingly shaped by the active participation of intelligent agents. - VNS
